title: Parameter-Efficient Models for Malaria Detection and Classification Using Small-Scale Imbalanced Blood Smear Images
text: Malaria screening faces a practical wall: severe class imbalance, datasets that hold only a few hundred images, and the cost of training separate models for every detection-classification pair. This study attacks all three at once. It builds a multi-model framework with a shared classification architecture, so classification models are trained once on ground-truth crops and reused across every detector.

title: Parameter-Efficient Models for Malaria Detection and Classification Using Small-Scale Imbalanced Blood Smear Images
text: Malaria screening faces a practical wall: severe class imbalance, datasets that hold only a few hundred images, and the cost of training separate models for every detection-classification pair. This study attacks all three at once. It builds a multi-model framework with a shared classification architecture, so classification models are trained once on ground-truth crops and reused across every detector.

title: Parameter-Efficient Models for Malaria Detection and Classification Using Small-Scale Imbalanced Blood Smear Images
text:
Findings

Detection: three YOLO Medium variants reached mAP@50 between 70.84% and 96.27%, with recall from 71.05% to 93.12%.
Classification: compact EfficientNet models (5.3M to 9.2M parameters) beat ResNet variants that use up to 44.5M parameters. EfficientNet-B1 hit 91.51% on the IML Lifecycle set and 98.28% on MP-IDB Species; ResNet50 reached 96.13% on the heavily imbalanced MP-IDB Stages set.
Imbalance handling: focal loss with alpha 1.0 and gamma 1.5 lifted F1 to between 0.44 and 1.00 on ultra-minority classes.
Deployment: models of 46 MB to 89 MB are small enough to run on resource-constrained hardware.

title: Parameter-Efficient Models for Malaria Detection and Classification Using Small-Scale Imbalanced Blood Smear Images
text:
Contribution

Shows that parameter-efficient architectures can match or beat much larger models on small, imbalanced medical datasets.
Offers a practical recipe for reusing one classification branch across many detectors.
Strengthens the case for affordable automated screening where expert microscopists are scarce.

title: Data Mining
text: An introduction to discovering useful patterns and knowledge from large datasets. The course covers the data-mining process, classification, clustering, association rules, and their application to real-world data.

title: Data Mining
text:
Topics

Data Mining Overview: the KDD process and data preprocessing.
Classification: decision trees, Naive Bayes, KNN, and ensemble methods.
Clustering: partitional (K-means) and hierarchical (agglomerative) methods.
Association Rules: frequent itemsets and Apriori.
Evaluation & Interpretation: measuring and interpreting mining results.
Applications: segmentation, anomaly detection, and market analysis.

title: Data Mining
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Apply the end-to-end data-mining process to a dataset.
Choose appropriate algorithms for classification, clustering, and association tasks.
Interpret and communicate discovered patterns.
Appreciate the ethical and privacy considerations of data mining.

Teaching Philosophy
I try to keep courses practical. We start with the math so the ideas are clear, then move quickly to notebooks and small projects that use local data. I also bring in examples from retail and media, where a model has to be reliable and easy to explain, not just accurate in a notebook.

title: Machine Learning
text: A practical, project-oriented course on machine learning. Students learn the full workflow, from data preparation and feature engineering to model selection, training, evaluation, and deployment, using Python.

title: Machine Learning
text:
Topics

Python for Data Science: NumPy, pandas, and visualization.
Data Preparation: cleaning, imputation, encoding, and scaling.
Supervised Learning: regression and classification (linear models, trees, ensembles, KNN).
Unsupervised Learning: clustering (K-means, hierarchical) and dimensionality reduction.
Model Evaluation: cross-validation, metrics, and hyperparameter tuning.
Deep Learning Introduction: neural networks and training basics.
Project: end-to-end machine-learning project on a real dataset.

title: Machine Learning
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Build complete machine-learning pipelines in Python.
Select and tune appropriate algorithms for a task.
Evaluate models rigorously and communicate results.
Recognize the practical considerations of deploying models in industry.

title: About
text:
I am Akhiyar Waladi, a lecturer (Asisten Ahli) in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Science and Technology, Universitas Jambi, where I teach and research topics in artificial intelligence, machine learning, pattern recognition, and predictive systems.
My path into computing started at IPB University (Institut Pertanian Bogor), where I earned my Bachelor of Computer Science in 2017. During my undergraduate years I explored embedded systems and computer vision, co-developing an Automated Fish Counter, an embedded system integrated with an Android device for automated fish measurement, counting, and sorting (showcased on Devpost). I continued to a Master of Computer Science at Universitas Indonesia (2018-2020), where I deepened my work on pattern recognition and machine learning, including research on automatic counting of scanned election forms using feature matching and convolutional neural networks.
Between 2018 and 2024 I worked in industry as a Data Scientist, first at kumparan (2018-2020) in Jakarta and then at Alfagift, Global Loyalty Indonesia (2020-2024) in Tangerang. In these roles I built and maintained data products, forecasting systems, recommendation and segmentation models, and end-to-end machine-learning pipelines used by millions of retail customers.
Since September 2024, I have been a lecturer at Universitas Jambi. I currently teach undergraduate courses in the electrical engineering program, supervise student projects, and lead community-service (pengabdian) programs that bring AI and IoT literacy to schools, pesantren, and vocational students in the Jambi region.

text:
Can the repository be private?
Yes, but it depends on your GitHub plan.



GitHub plan
Public repository + Pages
Private repository + Pages




GitHub Free (personal)
Yes
No


GitHub Free (organization)
Yes
No


GitHub Pro
Yes
Yes


GitHub Team
Yes
Yes


GitHub Enterprise Cloud
Yes
Yes



GitHub’s current documentation states that GitHub Pages is available from public repositories on GitHub Free, while public and private repositories are supported on GitHub Pro, Team, and Enterprise plans.
Official source:
https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages

Important distinction: private repository is not the same as private website
Even when the source repository is private, a normal GitHub Pages site is public on the internet by default. A truly privately published Pages site with access control requires an organization using GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
Official sources:

https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/creating-a-github-pages-site
https://docs.github.com/enterprise-cloud@latest/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/changing-the-visibility-of-your-github-pages-site



Recommendation for this portfolio
Use a public repository on GitHub Free.
That gives you:

free GitHub Pages hosting;
free GitHub Actions for a public repository;
an easy-to-inspect source history;
no server administration;
a natural place to keep the portfolio under version control.

A public academic website should contain only material that is already intended to be public. Never commit passwords, API keys, unpublished confidential material, student private data, internal documents, or sensitive files.
If someday you specifically want the website source hidden while the website remains public, GitHub Pro can host Pages from a private source repository.

title: Pengolahan Citra Digital
text: An undergraduate course on the theory and practice of digital image processing, taught in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Universitas Jambi. We start from how images are formed and stored, then work through enhancement, filtering, morphology, segmentation, and feature extraction, ending at the threshold where image processing hands off to machine learning.

title: Pengolahan Citra Digital
text:
Topics

Image representation: how a digital image is stored: pixels, color models, sampling, and quantization.
Point operations: brightness and contrast adjustment, histogram equalization.
Spatial filtering: smoothing, sharpening, and edge detection with convolution kernels.
Frequency-domain processing: the Fourier transform, filtering in the frequency domain.
Image restoration and enhancement: noise models, degradation, and reconstruction.
Morphological operations: erosion, dilation, opening, and closing.
Segmentation: thresholding, region-based and edge-based methods.
Feature extraction: descriptors that feed recognition and classification systems.

title: Pengolahan Citra Digital
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, students should be able to:

Explain how a digital image is formed and represented in memory.
Apply point, spatial, and frequency-domain techniques to improve image quality.
Use morphological and segmentation methods to isolate meaningful regions.
Extract features and build a simple image classification pipeline.
Implement core algorithms in Python using common image-processing libraries.

title: Pengolahan Citra Digital
text:
How This Connects to Research
The methods taught in this course show up directly in the research done in the department. Land-cover classification from Sentinel-2 imagery, malaria detection from microscopy images, and recognition of scanned documents all lean on the same building blocks: filtering, segmentation, and feature extraction. Students who finish this course have the foundation to read papers that apply these ideas.

title: Peningkatan Akurasi Klasifikasi Tutupan Lahan Menggunakan Random Forest pada Data Sentinel-2 di Jambi
text: Land-cover mapping supports environmental and agricultural planning. This study uses the Random Forest algorithm on Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to classify land cover across Jambi province, achieving improved accuracy over baseline methods.

title: Design and Development of a Multi-Blade Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine as an Alternative Energy Source in Talang Solok Regency
text: This project designs and develops a multi-blade horizontal axis wind turbine intended to supply electricity to households in Talang Solok Regency, Jambi. It is part of a broader effort to bring renewable energy options to rural communities where grid access is unreliable or absent.

Provides a locally documented example of small-scale wind power in Jambi.
